abilities.name: Attack
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target.
abilities._source: Convention: every class ships a free rank-1 Attack. It is also this class's only truly unconditional action, which matters more here than elsewhere - a Witch Hunter opens every fight on 0 Focus.

abilities.name: Shadowblast
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target. Generates 25 Focus.
abilities._source: CoA names Shadowblast in three of the four spec trees as the thing everything else is measured against (My Trusty Arbalest cuts its cost, Expert Shot raises its damage, Sharpshooter makes casting it restore resource, Darkrider cuts its cost again), so it is the class filler. THE FOCUS BUILDER: costs nothing, banks 25. Hunter's steady_shot curve exactly - 9 ranks, 42 rising to 124. Deliberately NOT gated on a ranged weapon, the same way none of Hunter's shots are, so the kit still functions unarmed.

abilities.name: Darkslayer
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target. Requires a ranged weapon.
abilities._source: CoA: Boltslinger's Heavy Crossbows 'increases the damage of Darkslayer by 50%, but increases its cast time by 0.5 sec' and Houndmaster's Silver Bullets and Darkhunter both scale it, so it is shared rather than spec-owned. The signature crossbow shot, so it is one of the few abilities that really does require the weapon.

abilities.name: Dawn Blade
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target.
abilities._source: CoA scales Dawn Blade from both Black Knight (Bulwark of Darkness, Destroyer of Evil, Undying, Dawn Knight, Foresight, Blade of the Misbegotten) and Inquisition (Protector of Darkshire, Interrogator, Dusk), so it is a class strike, not a spec one. The melee half of the chassis, on the same curve as Shadowblast.

abilities.name: Burrow Bolt
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Shoot a bolt with a rope attached to it at an enemy dealing AP Physical damage and pulling them to you'. Both Inquisition and Black Knight list it as a gap-closer. The pull itself has no engine hook - there is no position in a turn-based fight to drag anything to - so it lands as the damage half on a short cooldown.

abilities.name: Vault
abilities.description: Dodge +20 for 1 turn.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Dash in the direction you are moving. Distance scales with movement speed.' Movement is not a thing this engine models, so the dash lands as the brief window of not-being-where-the-attack-is that it buys. Free, because every spec's escape plan is built on having it.

abilities.name: Witching Shroud
abilities.description: Magic damage taken -50%, Immune to crowd control for 1 turn.
abilities._source: UNIT FIXED 2026-10-29: magic_damage_taken_pct was authored -0.5 as though it were a fraction, delivering -0.5% magic mitigation on an ability whose entire point is immunity to harmful magic. In an ABILITY's stat_mods this key is PERCENT POINTS - Character.take_damage divides the physical_/magic_ variants by 100, while the bare damage_taken_pct key four lines away in the same method is added undivided and IS a fraction. The convention is per-key with no naming rule. The fix was made in the emitted JSON earlier the same day and not ported here, so re-running this script silently restored the broken value.  CoA: 'Enter a powerful stealth mode for 3 seconds, granting immunity to all harmful magic effects... Usable while stunned or feared.' cc_immune is the engine's real crowd-control immunity flag (StatusEffectMixin reads it before applying a stun), paired with heavy magic mitigation. The 'only usable for 10 seconds after being hit by a magical critical strike' condition has no hook, so it is a plain 12-turn cooldown instead.

abilities.name: Witchblood Tonic
abilities.description: Removes 1 curse effect from an ally.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Drink a shadowy tonic, removing all curse effects from you and reducing all Magic damage taken by -40% for 10 seconds.' Both spec pages that mention it name only the cleanse ('Witchblood Tonic's curse cleanse'), so the cleanse is what it is - no effect_type does a dispel AND a buff in one cast, and the -40% magic window is dropped rather than faked. target_type 'ally' is the shipped convention for every friendly cleanse in the game.

abilities.name: Vampiric Tonic
abilities.description: Strengthens you for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Drink a vampiric tonic, allowing Physical damage dealt to heal you equal to 20% of the damage dealt for 10 seconds.' A real leech_pct proc carried on the buff's own StatusEffect, which is exactly 20% of the triggering hit. Three of the four spec pages call this the class's only real healing outside their own spec.

abilities.name: Slayer's Mark
abilities.description: Applies to the target: Physical damage taken +8% for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Mark an enemy, increasing the attack power of all attackers against that target by 150 and your critical strike chance against them by 3%.' A debuff's stat_mods land on the ENEMY here, so the attacker-side wording is turned round into the defender-side key that means the same thing - physical_damage_taken_pct on the marked target, read from status effects in Character.take_damage.  UNIT FIXED 2026-10-29: this was authored 0.08 as though the key were a fraction, so the mark increased damage taken by 0.08% - a debuff that did nothing. In an ABILITY's stat_mods this key is PERCENT POINTS (take_damage divides the physical_/magic_ variants by 100; the bare damage_taken_pct beside them is undivided and IS a fraction). The fix was made in the emitted JSON earlier the same day and not ported here, so re-running this script silently restored the broken value.

abilities.name: Inquisitor's Trap
abilities.description: Applies to up to 5 targets: Haste -25 for 2 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'a cruel trap... silencing them and all enemies in a 5 yd radius for 6 seconds.' There is no silence in this engine, and Guardian's Hammer of the Law set the precedent of NOT dressing a silence up as a stun, so it lands as a heavy haste debuff on the pack. The 'first enemy to approach' trigger has no hook either; it is cast.

abilities.name: Shadow Trap
abilities.description: Interrupts and stuns up to 5 targets for 1 turn.
abilities._source: CoA: 'stunning them for 4 seconds and dealing AP Shadow damage over 8 seconds'. The real stun - is_stun is only read in the debuff branch, so a stun has to be a debuff and cannot also be the DoT. Both Boltslinger and Inquisition cite the class traps as the only hard control they have ('stuns and silences come from class-kit traps an enemy has to walk into'), so the stun is the half that matters.

abilities.name: Death Trap
abilities.description: Deals Shadow damage to the target over time for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'a death trap... marking them for death, causing them to take AP Shadow damage after 1 minute.' A one-minute fuse is meaningless in turns, so it is a real Shadow DoT.

abilities.name: Noctis Blade
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target and heals you for part of it.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Strike an enemy, dealing 100% Weapon Damage plus 26, scaling with your parry rating, and healing you for 50% of the damage dealt.' The spec's whole identity - 'Noctis Blade is your on-demand self-heal, an active strike on a short cooldown whose damage and self-heal both scale with your parry rating.' damage_and_heal is the real effect_type for that. Scaling off parry specifically is not something an ability can declare, so the TREE does it: Dusk Knight converts Agility into parry and Dark Penance raises it.

abilities.name: Pommel Smash
abilities.description: Short, ugly, and it lands where the armour does not reach.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Pommel Smash strikes feed Shadowstorm, a chance to trigger a Shadowstorm burst', and Guardbreaker makes it cleave. The spec's cheap filler, so it is cheaper than Dawn Blade and has no cooldown.

abilities.name: Shadow Brand
abilities.description: Deals Shadow damage to the target over time for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Marks the target for 12 seconds, dealing 36 High Threat Shadow Damage over 12 seconds.' The 'High Threat' wording is why it carries a threat_generation_pct buff - percent POINTS as an ability stat_mod, unlike the tree's fractions. CoA applies it automatically off direct ability damage; nothing hooks that, so it is cast.

abilities.name: Guard Strike
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Bash an enemy with your weapon's hilt, interrupting them and preventing any spell from that school of magic from being cast for 3 seconds', and the spec blurb calls this 'the kit's only caster answer'. There is no interrupt and no school lockout in this engine, so the whole anti-caster half is gone and what remains is a cheap mid-cooldown strike. This is the single biggest gap between CoA's Black Knight and Frontier's.

abilities.name: Desecrate
abilities.description: Deals Shadow damage to up to 5 targets.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Desecrate up to 8 enemies in front of you, dealing Weapon Damage plus 18 as Shadow damage, piercing resistances. Only usable after avoiding an attack.' The avoidance gate has no hook - nothing records 'you just dodged' as a castable condition - so it is a plain cooldown. target_type enemy_aoe is what actually makes an ability hit more than one target; the is_aoe field several shipped files carry is never read.

abilities.name: Chains of Darkness
abilities.description: Applies to up to 5 targets: Taunts the target, Threat generated +200% for 2 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Pull all nearby enemies to you, dealing shadow AP Shadow damage and taunting them for 3 seconds', listed in the control suite as 'pull plus taunt to yank a target off an ally'. {'taunt': 1} is the engine's real taunt flag, handled in Ability.use rather than any one effect_type branch; the shipped tank taunts across Cultist, Starcaller, Venomancer and Primalist all use exactly this shape.

abilities.name: Stoicism
abilities.description: Damage taken -20% for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA never prints Stoicism's own tooltip, but two Black Knight talents exist only to modify it (Calm Under Pressure cuts its cooldown by 30 sec, Dark Barrier extends it by 5 sec), which makes it a real mitigation cooldown. Sized below Guardian's Raise Shield (-40%) because this spec gets Gaze of the Black Knight on top.

abilities.name: March of the Black King
abilities.description: Restores focus to you.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Expel darkness from within you, dealing 55 Shadow damage to nearby enemies over 10 seconds. Generates 5 Rage every 2 sec', and the spec's strengths say 'March of the Black King refunds Rage. You rarely go dry.' Frontier's Focus is CoA's Rage here (see the module docstring), so this is the tank's own Focus refill. NOTE the engine reads mana_restore_pct OFF THE RANK for restore_resource, not effect_value - Guardian's Knight's Calling omits it and restores 0.

abilities.name: Knight's Seal
abilities.description: Deals Shadow damage to the target over time for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Curse an enemy, dealing shadow AP Shadow damage every 2 sec and applying Dark Oath to you, reducing all damage taken by 5% for 8 seconds.' A single cast cannot both DoT an enemy and buff the caster, so the Dark Oath half is dropped and the DoT kept.

abilities.name: Witching Idol
abilities.description: Removes 2 magic effects from an ally.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Drop a Witching Idol that periodically dispels fear, sleep, and charm effects every 3 sec from party members within 20 yds.' DispelType has only magic/curse/poison/disease, and fear, sleep and charm are all Magic effects in WoW, so it cleanses Magic - two at a time, standing in for the periodic tick, which has no hook.

abilities.name: Witchblight
abilities.description: Deals Shadow damage to up to 5 targets and heals you for part of it.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Explode with dark energy, dealing shadow AP Shadow damage to up to 10 enemies within 8 yds and healing you for 20% of your maximum health. Each target struck is guaranteed to miss their next instance of damage.' damage_and_heal carries the damage and the self-heal; the guaranteed-miss rider has no hook.

abilities.name: Gaze of the Black Knight
abilities.description: Damage taken -15% for 3 turns, absorbing damage.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Apply a dark shield to yourself, absorbing AP damage and then gaze upon your party members, causing 25% of the damage they take to be transferred to you for 12 seconds.' The absorb is real (absorb_pct_max_health is read for cast buffs). The party-damage REDIRECTION is not expressible - no effect routes one combatant's incoming damage to another - so the mitigation lands on the Black Knight instead. CoA calls this 'rare group damage-redirection' and 'one long-cooldown panic button', and it is the spec's one real loss in translation.

abilities.name: Tormentor
abilities.description: Deals Shadow/Arcane damage to the target over time for 3 turns. Requires a ranged weapon.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Fire a deadly bolt dealing Twilight Damage plus ranged AP over 14 seconds', and the rotation opens with it - 'Open with Tormentor to lay its DoT'. Twilight is shadow-arcane (see TWILIGHT). CoA explicitly lists it among the abilities that 'want a ranged crossbow equipped'.

abilities.name: Witchbane
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target over time for 3 turns. Requires a ranged weapon.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Unleash a series of devastating shots dealing ranged AP Physical damage over 3 seconds' - a channel, so a physical DoT rather than one hit. Arbalest Mastery ('each subsequent shot deals 15% more') and Rapid ('full damage over 1 second shorter') both scale it in the tree.

abilities.name: Heartseeking Bolt
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target. Requires a ranged weapon.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Charge up a powerful bolt that deals 200% Ranged Weapon Damage plus shadow SP to an enemy and reduces their healing received by 30% for 10 seconds.' The spec's payoff button - 'build Bounty Hunter stacks... then spend them on a charged Heartseeking Bolt for burst'. The anti-heal rider is a debuff and a damage cast cannot carry one, so it is dropped; healing_taken_pct exists but only as a debuff's own stat_mods.

abilities.name: Twilight Frenzy
abilities.description: Deals Shadow/Arcane damage to up to 5 targets. Requires a ranged weapon.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Spin around, unable to stop moving for 5 seconds, firing shots at nearby enemies for 50% Ranged Weapon Damage plus as Twilight Damage. Can dodge and parry while active.' The spec's cleave. Evasive and Crossbow Frenzy in the tree are what CoA layers on top of it.

abilities.name: Damnation
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target. Requires a ranged weapon. Usable only below 35% health.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Deplete your rage to shoot a powerful bolt... converting each point of Rage into additional damage. Only usable on enemies below 35% health.' execute_threshold_pct is PERCENT in this engine (Warrior's Execute 20, Netherstrike and Electrocute 35), matching CoA's 35 exactly. 'Deplete your rage' is not a cost shape the engine has - costs are fixed per rank - so it costs the most Focus of anything in the class instead.

abilities.name: Daring Escape
abilities.description: Dodge +30 for 1 turn.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Jump backwards, causing all ranged attacks to miss you for 2 seconds.' Nothing distinguishes incoming RANGED attacks from melee ones, so the guaranteed miss becomes a large dodge window - the strongest one in the class, which is right for a spec whose summary is 'not being caught is the defense'.

abilities.name: Pavise
abilities.description: Drive the shield into the dirt and work from behind it.
abilities._source: CoA: Pavise Crossbowman 'teaches you how to use Shields and teaches you Pavise. Slam your shield into the ground, forming a pavise for 10 sec. While you remain near it, hostile spells targeting you are deflected.' The shield proficiency half is already true - weapon_types.json gives Witch Hunter shields - and spell deflection has no hook, so it lands as a real absorb. Authored at level 44 rather than talent-unlocked so the spec has it without spending its capstone, and the tree's Dead and Gone extends it.

abilities.name: Slayer
abilities.description: Grants your party: Physical crit chance +3, Spell crit chance +3 for 4 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Increases critical strike chance of all party and raid members by 3%... In addition, increases your critical strike chance by 3%.' The raid buff the spec's own blurb sells it on ('brings raid crit (Slayer)'). target_type 'party' with buff_scope 'combat' is the shipped shape for a real party buff; buff_scope only accepts 'raid' or 'combat' and silently rewrites anything else.

abilities.name: Houndmaster's Whistle
abilities.description: Summons a pet to fight for you.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Summons a permanent Shadowhound companion to aid you in combat. Your Shadowhound receives 25% of healing done to you.' NOW A REAL SHADOWHOUND. This pointed at 'wolf' and summoned a pet named Wolf - the most defensible of the mismatches fixed in Oct 2026, since a houndmaster's hound really is wolf-shaped, but CoA names the creature so it gets its own template. Built deliberately CLOSE to the wolf it replaced (130 health against 140, comparable damage) because that mapping was never a power problem, only a naming one. The healing redirect has no hook - a pet cannot reach its owner, which is the same gap the Wolf's own Furious Howl is approximated around. effect_type 'summon' summons NOTHING - four Tinker abilities shipped that way and were silently empty for months.

abilities.name: Unleash the Hounds
abilities.description: Summons a pet to fight for you.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Summon 1 Lesser Shadow Hound to aid you in combat for 20 seconds', with Kennel Master adding more. NOW A REAL LESSER SHADOWHOUND: this pointed at 'raptor' and summoned the Primalist's tameable beast on a Witch Hunter. The template is authored LESSER, as CoA says - plainly weaker than this class's own permanent Shadowhound in every stat. FIXED 2026-10-29, and the fix was in two places: Character.EXTRA_PET_CAP had no Witch Hunter entry, so max_extra_pets was 0 and Character.summon_pet ignored additional=True entirely - this level-20 button REPLACED the level-1 permanent Shadowhound with the weaker one, a button that downgraded you. The cap now carries 'Witch Hunter': 2, so additional_pet=True here is live data and both hounds field at once. CoA reads as a board anyway (Houndmaster's Call and Rampaging Hounds both say 'Hounds', plural).

abilities.name: Quickdraw
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target. Generates 25 Focus.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Unleash a quick shot, dealing 175% Ranged Weapon Damage plus ranged AP Physical damage and generates Rage. Only usable after critically striking with an ability.' The crit gate has no hook, so it is a 2-turn cooldown instead - and the Rage generation is real, which makes this the spec's own Focus builder alongside Shadowblast.

abilities.name: Houndmaster's Call
abilities.description: Deals Shadow damage to the target.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Command your Shadow Hounds to leap upon an enemy target, dealing two strikes for ranged AP Shadow damage.' A pet cannot be ordered to strike from the owner's cast in this engine, so the hounds' damage resolves as the owner's Shadow strike. Expulsion of Evil in the tree resets it.

abilities.name: Darkflock
abilities.description: Deals Shadow damage to up to 5 targets over time for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Channel for 8 seconds, commanding a flock of crows to deal SP Shadow damage to enemies in a wide cone every 2 sec. Can channel while moving.' spell_dot because CoA scales it off spell power, not AP - the spec's stat priority lists Spell Power for exactly this ('feeds the minor Shadow portions of Darkflock/Feast of Talons').

abilities.name: Repulse
abilities.description: Deals Shadow damage to up to 4 targets.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Emit a burst of shadow from your musket that strikes enemies in front of you, dealing 57 Shadow damage and knocking all affected targets back.' The spec blurb calls it 'a frontal knockback' and its only on-demand control. There is no knockback and no position, so what survives is the cone damage.

abilities.name: Decimate
abilities.description: Attack Power Pct +15%, Haste +8 for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Empowers your Shadow Hounds for 20 seconds, granting them 30% increased damage and haste and allowing them to ignore Armor.' A cast buff cannot reach the pet: Pet reads its owner's pet_damage/pet_health/pet_armor TALENTS when it is built, and nothing else, so a temporary buff on the owner never touches it. The talent tree carries the real hound scaling (Dark Ranger, Loksey's Journal, Decimate's own node, Lethal Pursuit) and this ability keeps the burst window on the Houndmaster instead.

abilities.name: Darkfeast
abilities.description: Heals you.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Darkfeast is your on-demand heal.' The spec's weaknesses are blunt about it being nearly all the healing there is, so it is a real heal on a long cooldown rather than a trickle. Hunter's Revive Pet curve, scaled down.

abilities.name: Rearmament
abilities.description: Resets your ability cooldowns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Arm yourself against evil, resetting the cooldown of all Traps and Decimate', and the spec blurb leads with it - 'your Trap spells, reset on demand by Rearmament'. reset_cooldowns is a real effect_type; it does not take a filter, so it resets the whole book rather than only the traps, which is why its own cooldown is the longest in the class.

abilities.name: Smite Evil
abilities.description: Deals Holy damage to up to 3 targets.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Strike an enemy with your blade, dealing Weapon Damage plus 25 as Holy damage to them and 5 nearby enemies.' The spec's cheap cleaving filler; Flames of the Sinned in the tree gives it a chance to strike twice.

abilities.name: Dusk Blade
abilities.description: Deals Shadow damage to the target and heals you for part of it.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Strike an enemy with both weapons, dealing Weapon Damage plus shadow SP Shadow damage, piercing resistances. Heals for 25% of damage dealt.' The spec's sustain - 'Dusk Blade is your health siphon' and 'the payoff is... grinding a fight out with Dusk Blade's siphon'.

abilities.name: Purifier's Edge
abilities.description: Deals Fire damage to the target.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Strike an enemy with searing blades, dealing Weapon Damage plus 20 with both weapons as Fire damage. Grants Flames of Sin or increases the duration by 3 sec.' Flames of Sin is a stacking auto-attack rider with no engine shape; the tree's Searing Hilt carries the attack-speed half instead.

abilities.name: Torchlight
abilities.description: Deals Fire damage to the target.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Throw a torch at an enemy, dealing fire SP Fire damage, and causing up to 5 of the next attacks you make against them to grant you Flames of Sin.' spell_damage because CoA gives it an SP coefficient and the spec's stat priority puts Spell Power above Agility for exactly this group of casts. Sinner and Dawn in the tree are its payoff nodes.

abilities.name: Fiery Judgement
abilities.description: Deals Fire damage to up to 4 targets.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Judge an enemy, dealing fire SP Fire damage to them and nearby enemies.' The spell-power-scaled AoE half of the fire kit; Cinder and Ashes raises its SP scaling.

abilities.name: Flourish
abilities.description: Deals Fire damage to up to 4 targets.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Perform an advanced flourish, dealing AP Fire damage to nearby enemies, repeating every 4 sec, and causing your Flames of Sin to cleave up to 3 additional enemies for 20 seconds.' The repeat and the Flames cleave have no hook; the AoE strike does.

abilities.name: Hunt
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Charge an enemy, slowing their movement speed by -70% for 2 seconds and generating 20 Rage. 2 Charges, 25 sec recharge.' Neither charges nor movement speed exist here, so it is a cheap gap-closer on a real cooldown - and the tree's The Hunt Continues carries the Focus generation CoA puts on the ability itself.

abilities.name: Stake
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target. Usable only below 35% health.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Drive your concealed stake into the chest of an injured enemy, dealing AP Physical damage... Only usable on enemies at or below 35% health.' The spec's execute, at CoA's own 35.

abilities.name: Darkslayer's Lantern
abilities.description: Interrupts and stuns up to 5 targets for 1 turn.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Empower a lantern with your Flames of Sin and let it shine, dealing AP Fire damage and stunning all enemies within 5 yds for 5 seconds', described in the strengths as 'an AoE stun for locking down a pack'. A stun has to be a debuff for is_stun to be read, so the Fire damage half is dropped and the stun kept - the stun is what the rotation presses it for.

abilities.name: Pyro Tonic
abilities.description: Damage dealt +20% for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Drink a fiery tonic, increasing your Fire damage dealt by 20% and your critical damage by 10% for 15 seconds.' damage_dealt_pct is the engine's one generic outgoing-damage buff key and it is PERCENT POINTS (divided by 100 in _damage_multiplier), unlike the tree's fire keys. There is no fire-only buff key - the per-school damage keys are talent-only - so 20% lands on all of the Inquisitor's damage rather than just the Fire half.

abilities.name: Monster Hunting
abilities.description: Grants your party: Haste +10 for 4 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Increases melee and ranged haste of party and raid members within 100 yds by 10%.' The raid buff the spec's S-tier raid rating is partly sold on ('brings raid haste (Monster Hunting)'). The '+10% damage against Undead and Demons' half has no creature-type hook.
